title: Ice Floats? Hydrogen Bonding Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Ice floats on water, water boils only at 100 °C, and the two strands of DNA stay zipped. One tiny pull explains all three. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) Diya drops an ice cube into water and we find out why it floats.

You will see electronegativity as a tug of war, watch fluorine pull the shared pair away from hydrogen to make δ+ and δ-, and see HF molecules link into a zig zag chain on the molecule bench. We compare intermolecular hydrogen bonds (water, HF, alcohols) with the intramolecular bond in o-nitrophenol, work out which of CH4, NH3, H2S and CH3OH form hydrogen bonds, compare boiling points (H2O 100 °C, H2S about -60 °C) and watch ice lock into open rings. Then the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 50 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three puzzles, one pull
0:25 Tug of war: electronegativity
1:03 The molecule bench: HF chain
1:50 Intermolecular vs intramolecular
2:20 Pause and think: ortho or para?
2:44 Worked example: who forms H-bonds?
3:27 Why ice floats
4:01 Exam trap and where it is asked
4:24 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:01 Recap and three questions
